run.question: Fetch me the logs for the inventory-service pod in namespace app-102

report.summary: The requested pod exists and its logs were retrieved. Pod inventory-service-7ff7d5959f-nmfh6 in namespace app-102 is Running and owned by ReplicaSet inventory-service-7ff7d5959; both its containers (inventory-service, promtail) are ready with restart count 0, and the pod started at 2026-11-23T18:51:59Z with the inventory-service container started at 18:52:00Z. Reading the pod's own container logs returned 8 lines, all from the promtail sidecar (stdout/startup banner and Promtail tailing /var/log/inventory.log); the inventory-service container's own stdout stream returned 0 lines, and neither container had a previous instance. The application log content was therefore taken from Loki, which returned 8 lines for namespace app-102 between 2026-11-23T18:52:01.607Z and 2026-11-23T18:52:34.129Z from stream job=inventory-service, pod_name=inventory-service-7ff7d5959f-nmfh6, filename=/var/log/inventory.log: order and stock events, one WARN 'Low stock warning for ITEM-9999 - current level: 5 units', an INFO reconciliation '127 items verified', and periodic INFO 'Inventory check completed - all systems operational' lines. A Loki line filter for error|fail|exception|panic|timeout over the same hour returned nothing; because that view is no_data it is recorded as a query that matched nothing, not as proof that no errors occurred. No fault was diagnosed and no root cause is asserted.

next_steps: If logs from before 2026-11-23T18:51:59Z are needed, query Loki over a wider window with the selector {namespace="app-102", job="inventory-service"} (Loki may retain lines for pods that no longer exist), since the pod's own container logs do not.

To confirm whether any error lines exist, re-run the Loki error filter with broader patterns and a larger limit, or check log levels via a metric query such as sum by (level) (count_over_time({namespace="app-102", job="inventory-service"}[15m])), rather than relying on the single no_data result.
If the 'Low stock warning for ITEM-9999 - current level: 5 units' WARN matters, review inventory levels for ITEM-9999 rather than treating it as a service fault.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
